title: Elderberry Wine
statementMd:
Jeanne and her son Semi-Demi-John are engaged in the elderberry-wine making business.

The recipe requires, aside from a closely-guarded secret quantity of the letter 𝑟r, strict proportions of 1212 parts fresh elderberries, 1212 parts brewing sugar, and 4040 parts water. As long as one or more ingredients are lacking, the team will place an order for as much extra as needed to make up the weight, and start again.

For instance:

- If they have 1818kg of elderberries, 99kg of sugar, and 100100kg of water, they can use 99kg of elderberries, all 99kg of the sugar, and 3030kg of the water and then they are stuck.
- They must then order 99kg more of sugar in order to proceed and use 99kg, 99kg, and 3030kg again.
- After this they must order 1212kg each of elderberries and sugar in order to finally use 1212kg, 1212kg, and 4040kg of elderberries, sugar, and water respectively.

## Input

The input consists of one line containing three floating-point numbers 𝑎a, 𝑏b, 𝑐c (0≤𝑎,𝑏,𝑐≤10160≤a,b,c≤1016): the number of kilograms of elderberries, sugar, and water respectively.

## Output

Output three floating-point numbers 𝑎′a′ 𝑏′b′ 𝑐′c′ giving the cumulative total quantities of elderberries, sugar, and water that will be ordered respectively.

The output must be accurate to an absolute or relative error of 10−610−6.
